ai_provisions: The Institutes intend to develop an interoperable programme of work and approach to safety research.
They intend to develop a shared approach to model evaluations, including methodologies, infrastructures and processes.
They intend to perform at least one joint testing exercise on a publicly accessible model.
They intend to collaborate on AI safety technical research and to explore personnel exchanges.
They intend to share information across their activities, subject to national laws, regulations and contracts.
The partners intend to work with other governments on international standards for AI safety testing and related standards.
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding bilateral cooperation on AI safety science and institute-to-institute work. No treaty obligation, ratification, depositary, dispute settlement or enforcement; no general AI regulation or military-AI commitment.
relevance.reason: A bilateral government memorandum of understanding on AI safety science, signed on 1 April 2024 by the UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology and the US Secretary of Commerce. It provides the basis for cooperation between the UK and US AI Safety Institutes on model evaluations, joint testing, technical research, personnel exchanges and information sharing. It is a non-binding MOU, not a treaty, and the official GOV.UK publication is a summary of key elements rather than the full MOU text.
